tagline.text: A Cebu canyon descent from the upper Kanlaob River to Kawasan Falls

location.label: Location
location.text: Kanlaob River area, Barangay Compostela, Alegria, southwestern Cebu

children.text: This canyoneering route starts on the upper Kanlaob River in Alegria, southwestern Cebu, and takes you downstream by walking, swimming and jumping all the way to Kawasan Falls in Badian. Starting from the Alegria side adds blue pools, a long natural slide and higher cliff sections.
Alegria is a quiet municipality on the southwestern coast of Cebu, facing the Tañon Strait. It lies about

from Cebu City. The town center is by the sea, but canyoneering begins inland, in the hills around the Kanlaob River in Barangay Compostela. On the Badian side the same river is also called the Matutinao River, and at its downstream end lies the famous Kawasan Falls.

The simplest way to think of Alegria canyoneering is as the upper part of the usual Kawasan canyoneering. The standard route from Badian starts partway down the river, while starting in Alegria means you also cover the stretch above it. A 2018 travel blog said the Alegria section has five or six more big jumps that Badian-only visitors miss, with taller canyon walls and deeper blue water. It described the two groups as joining up about 45 minutes after the start.

The activities include canyon trekking, floating with the current, natural water slides, crawling through narrow gaps and waterfall jumps. Many operators say you can take part even if you cannot swim because you wear a life vest, but people who are very afraid of water may find it hard. Most jumps are optional, so if you are scared you can walk or take a bypass down instead. Inside the canyon the guide tells you where to jump and how, and some operators also have a safety crew member follow at the back. Groups are generally described as having one guide for every four guests. For first-timers, we recommend making Alegria canyoneering the center of your day and spending the afternoon relaxing at Kawasan Falls or moving on to Moalboal. Canyoneering is tiring and you finish wet, so avoid stacking a long transfer on the same day. If you start in the morning you will finish in the early afternoon, which leaves plenty of time to reach Moalboal's beaches or Cebu City that same day.

Operating status changes with the season, so be sure to check. Alegria and Badian have at times handled entry and operations separately. A 2026 guide says the Alegria extension is suspended for safety reasons, while some operators are still selling Alegria-start tours for dates in that same period. Before you set out, ask an operator or the Alegria tourism office.

blocks.title: Start on the upper Kanlaob River

children.text: The Alegria start is the deepest and quietest part of the canyon. Before the Badian tour groups join in, there are few people, which also makes it a good place for photos.
One operator lists 9 major jumps of
plus a rope swing, while another says 7. Only the
1m
jump is required and the rest are optional. How high a jump feels depends on the water level.
Deep blue-green pools made by mineral-rich water follow one after another, and reviewers say the Alegria section has the longest natural water slide on the course.
The route ends at the second level of Kawasan Falls in Badian, and one guide says it finishes with a jump of about
(45 feet) there. That jump is optional too. Afterward you can swim at the first level of the falls.

Some operators offer a lower-priced option that goes only to Kanlaob Falls without canyoneering, which suits companions or small children who do not want to jump. Prices vary by operator and group size, so check what is included when you book.
Badian town is crowded with group tours all day, but the Cebu provincial tourism site describes Alegria as less commercialized. At the starting point you can feel the calm of a small town.
Arrive at the registration office in Alegria or Badian. According to one operator, arriving around this time gives you a relaxed start to get your gear.
Register, put on your gear (helmet, life vest, shoes) and take the safety briefing. Some operators give you a waterproof wristband as your entry ticket.
Ride a habal-habal or shuttle for about
5–10 minutes
to the start point.
Canyoneering begins. You make your way downstream alternating between walking, swimming, jumping and sliding.
Swim at the second and first levels of Kawasan Falls. Depending on the operator, you may also stop at the nearby Kabukalan spring.
Return to the headquarters, shower, change clothes and have lunch (inclusion varies by operator).
These times are one operator's sample schedule, and the whole trip takes
3–6 hours
depending on group size and photo stops. The earlier you start, the fewer people and the cooler it is.
If you have children or do not want to jump, choose a package that goes only from the headquarters to Kanlaob Falls.
Enjoy the pool below the falls. Some operators have children aged 4–6 wait here with a parent or guide.
Return to the headquarters for lunch and a rest.
A direct flight from Manila (NAIA) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change often, so check before booking.
From the airport, take a taxi to the South Bus Terminal in Cebu City, or use an operator's hotel pickup package.
There is no single connection from Manila to Alegria, so the usual approach is to fly to Cebu first and then continue south by road.
From the South Bus Terminal, take a Ceres or Librando bus marked "Bato via Barili" and get off at Alegria town, Matutinao or Madridejos.
The trip takes about
3 hours 30 minutes–5 hours
and the fare is about
depending on the source and whether the bus is air-conditioned. Note that "Bato via Oslob" buses take a different road.
Tell the bus conductor in advance where you want to get off.

items.title: From the drop-off to the start point

children.text: From where you get off, take a habal-habal to the registration office in the Compostela area or to the operator's headquarters.
If you start from the Badian side, a habal-habal from near Matutinao Church to the headquarters sometimes costs about
Some day tours pick you up by private vehicle from hotels in Mactan, Cebu City, Moalboal, Oslob and Badian, and prices vary widely with distance, from
If you travel on your own, a local bus from Moalboal takes about
30 minutes–1 hour
The dry season from November to May is best. The water is clear, the level is stable and it is safer, and March to May is peak season, so weekend slots fill up fast.

Tours do run on some days in the rainy season (June to October), but sudden rising water after heavy rain means cancellations are common. One operator lists the third Wednesday of each month as a river cleanup day and Good Friday as closed, so check when you set your date.

Even within November to May, Monday to Thursday is said to be the quietest. On the other hand, weekends and holidays from March to May bring large crowds and long waits, so arrive early to finish registration.

Alegria has small places to stay such as Alegria Waterfront Beach House, Alegria Dive Resort and CocoVille Guesthouse. If you want more facilities, many people stay in Moalboal, about
30–45 minutes
from Alegria.

Meals are often a Filipino buffet or lunch included in the operator package, though what is included differs by operator. In town you can eat Cebuano food such as grilled seafood, pork barbecue, kinilaw and noodle soups. Bring plenty of cash, as the town reportedly has few ATMs and many places do not take cards.

After canyoneering you get quite cold, so a meal with a hot soup is a good idea. There are simple eateries near the operators' headquarters and many packages include lunch. Local operators also sell a meal as an option, made up of two dishes, unlimited rice and a drink.
Book through an operator or local guide, and confirm ahead for peak season and weekends.
An early start (6–8 AM) is best, with fewer people and cooler weather.
You need water shoes that stay on your feet or sandals with straps. Flip-flops are not allowed, and operators sometimes lend shoes.
Many operator headquarters have shower and changing areas. Bring a change of clothes and a plastic bag so you do not ride the bus soaking wet.
Bring swimwear, a towel, a change of clothes and a waterproof phone case. Leave valuables and jewelry behind.
Apply sunscreen before you arrive. If it washes off in the water it is a nuisance.
Every jump is optional. Do not push yourself, and follow the guide's signals.
Giving a small tip to guides and porters is customary. Tips are often not included in the package.
Check the notices for the Kanlaob and Matutinao areas on the day and ask whether tours are running before you set out.
If you want to rest at the first level of Kawasan Falls after canyoneering, do not delay lunch and leave some room in your schedule.
After rain the canyon can suddenly flood and become dangerous. Operations may be suspended or the route may change, so be sure to check local notices.
Many operators do not allow children under 7 to canyoneer, and children must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.
It is not recommended for people with medical conditions such as high blood pressure or epilepsy, or with limited mobility.
Entering the canyon without a guide when the water is rising is dangerous, so always go with a guide.
There are many slippery rocks, so do not walk without shoes.
Alegria and Badian have at times operated differently, so do not mix up the registration offices, and confirm the start point when you book.
Mobile signal is weak in some places and you may lose contact inside the canyon. Agree on a meeting place with your group beforehand.
The end of the canyoneering route, an emerald three-level waterfall reachable on foot. Bamboo rafting is also available.
